jordan (Support): Hey team, high-priority from Acme-Data: since they bumped max_batch_size -> 256 yesterday, we're seeing intermittent 'dimension mismatch' errors from the embeddings route and a big tail-latency spike. They also reported a billing surge due to retries. Root symptoms: some embedding responses with dim 0, others normal (expected 768), tail p95/p99 up ~+1.8s. Happened around the same time their API token rotation ran.
ajhwin (typo to correct)
ashwin (Eng-ML): Can you paste the exact route, model, and a sample request+headers? Also need the batcher trace and a small server log snippet with batch ids. Any client-side batching or custom SDK logic?
jordan (Support): Model: open-embed-large-v2, endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings. Customer increased max_batch_size from 128 -> 256 on their Dedicated pool. They did a token rotation via console at 2026-03-16T03:14:xx UTC. Sample curl we used to repro:

```bash
for i in $(seq 1 500); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
    -H "X-RW-Debug: batch-trace" \ 
    -d '{"model":"open-embed-large-v2","input":"test line '$i'"}' &
done
wait
```

We captured batch traces and a few error lines. Example error: "Embedding result dimension 0 != expected 768" and occasional 401s around the token rotation window. Also saw a billing jump from retries.

ashwin (Eng-ML): That trace header is good. Please paste one representative batch-trace line and the short worker log around the batch id.

jordan (Support): Batch trace snippet (sanitized):

```
BATCH_TRACE: batch_id=bd123 worker=shard-7 model_variant=fp16_q4_0 items=14 dims=[768,768,0,768,768,0,768,768,768,768,768,768,768,768] flush_ms=10
```

Worker log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-16T03:14:15Z] auth: WARN token revoked for client_id=acme-123
[2026-03-16T03:14:16Z] embed-worker[shard-7]: ERROR: partial result for batch bd123 (item 3 empty)
[2026-03-16T03:14:18Z] node-kernel: killed process pid=19123 due to OOM
```

So some items returned dim 0. There are both auth warnings and an OOM around the same timeframe.

sam_k (Eng-Platform): Ok this looks like a collision of events: dynamic batching + token rotation + a worker instability. If a worker gets an auth failure mid-batch or gets OOM-killed while serializing outputs, downstream code might emit empty/truncated embeddings (dim 0). When max_batch_size is larger, each batch holds more items so a single failure affects more requests -> amplified tail and billing due to retries. Also token rotation can cause transient 401s on in-flight requests.

maria (Customer Success): Customer says they only changed max_batch_size to try to increase throughput. They want a quick mitigation (they're on Dedicated). They reported the billing spike and are unhappy.

ashwin (Eng-ML): Short repro steps for us to confirm locally:
1) set max_batch_size=256 and dynamic_batch_flush_ms=10 on a dev pool
2) run the curl loop above with a background token rotate (simulate revocation)
3) collect X-RW-Debug traces and worker logs filtered by batch_id

Also try running the load with intentionally empty strings every ~10th request to rule out client blank inputs.

jordan (Support): I ran the quick check. When we roll max_batch_size back to 128 the incidence drops dramatically. With 256 we saw repeated batch_ids with mixed dims. Sample trace shows dims with zeros mixed in the middle which matches worker partial failures.

sam_k (Eng-Platform): Proposed immediate mitigations (short-term):
- Roll back max_batch_size -> 128 (already reduced impact)
- Reduce dynamic_batch_flush_ms to 2ms to keep batches smaller under bursty traffic
- Server-side validate and reject empty inputs (respond 400) before batching
- Add a guard: if auth failure occurs for a single item in the batch, fail whole batch with explicit 401/429 so clients don't silently get empty embeddings

Longer-term: avoid partial success semantics for batcher outputs, improve atomicity of batch serialization, and harden worker OOM handling + backpressure.

billing-bot: FYI invoice link: https://billing.redwood.ai/invoices/0x9f3 shows request counts spiking at 2026-03-16T03:12 - 03:20 UTC. If you want to issue a goodwill credit, ping billing@redwood.

infra-watchdog: Noted node oom and restart on pool-dedicated-3 at 03:14:18Z, investigating underlying host memory pressure. Eviction likely due to background model loads + larger batch footprints.

maria (Customer Success): Customer agreed to rollback to 128 and asks for a postmortem and ETA on permanent fix. They also want a small credit applied for the retry-driven billing spike.

ashwin (Eng-ML): I'll open ENG-12345 (batcher-atomicity) and ENG-12346 (auth-handling-midbatch) and assign owners. For immediate follow-up I'll watch the dev pool traces after rollback. Jordan, can you run the reproducible script one more time with rollback and paste the new batch-traces? If dims are stable we'll close the escalation and schedule the follow-up work.

jordan (Support): Will do and post traces. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
